newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil drifts sideways.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil drifts sideways.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps drifted sideways late afternoon on Monday in quiet trading after opening up about 30 cents on firmer crude values and improved fundamentals, traders said.
"Gas oil is very quiet. It is waiting for direction from the physical market," one trader said.
March gas oil swap bids were last quoted at $26.30/$26.40 per barrel up from Friday's $26.00/$26.10, on talks that $26.30 traded earlier in the day.
April was last quoted at $26.10/$26.20 per barrel, also up about 20 cents from Friday. The March/April spread was valued at an unchanged plus 20 cents, they said.

Traders said firmer prices were due in part to tighter physical supplies in Singapore following the sale of three 30,000-tonne cargoes to Thailand and a total of 80,000-tonnes to India and Bangladesh.
China also emerged with purchase enquiries for March cargoes but at lower levels, with barge lot sales on an ex-Hong Kong basis to southern China now picking up after the Lunar New Year lull.
Swaps were also boosted by a firmer gas oil futures open on the International Petroleum Exchange where March last traded up $1.50 per tonne to $179.75.
The jet fuel market was steady with the March regrade bid seen at $2.40 per barrel up from Friday's at $2.00/$2.30, brokers said.
Brokers said the market firmed following large purchases by airlines who came out to buy the swaps early last week to lock in their costs.
Fuel oil swaps firmed in line with fresh physical buying interest from China, India and Pakistan.
Sentiment also has improved on exports to Thailand and a larger purchase from Taiwan which bought a total of 114,000 tonnes for March arrival.
March bids were last quoted at $103.50/$105.00 per tonne, from Friday's $103.00/$104.00 per tonne.
